G0165G.as:
αἰών, -ῶνος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for עַד ,עוֹלָם;]
1. in cl., like Lat. aevum (LS, MM, VGT, s.v.), a space of time, as, a lifetime, generation, period of history, an indefinitely long period; in NT of an indefinitely long period, an age, eternity, usually c. prep. (MM, VGT);
(a) of the past: ἀπ’ αἰ. (cf. Heb. מֵעוֹלָם), ;
(b) of the future: εἰς τ. αἰ. (cf. לְעוֹלָם), forever, ; id., c. neg., never, ; more strongly, εἰς τὸν αἰ. τοῦ αἰ., (LXX); εἰς τοὺς αἰ., ; εἰς τοὺς αἰ. τῶν αἰ. (cf. Is 45:17, עַד־עוֹלְמֵי עַד), , LT; cf. also , , , .
2. οἱ αἰ., the worlds, the universe, "the sum of the periods of time, including all that is manifested in them": (cf. , where τῶν αἰ. are prob. "the ages or world-periods which when summed up make eternity".
3. the present age (Heb. הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה): ὁ αἰ., ; ὁ αἰ. οὗτος, ; ὁ νῦν αἰ., ; ὁ ἐνεστὼς αἰ., ; similarly, of the time after Christ's second coming (הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא), ὁ αἰ. ἐκεῖνος, ; ὁ αἰ. μέλλων, ; ὁ αἰ. ὁ ἐρχόμενος, .
SYN.: κόσμος, the ordered universe, the scheme of material things; οἰκουμένη, the inhabited earth; in contrast with both of which αἰ. is the world under aspects of time (cf. Westc. on ; Tr., Syn., §lix; Thayer, s.v., αἰ.; Cremer, 74, 620; MM, VGT).
